name: spot

# Spot the problems 🔍

A collaborator sends you `messy_samples.csv`:

```{r spot.file, echo=FALSE, comment=""}
cat(readLines("data/slide_loading_data/messy_samples.csv"), sep = "\n")
```

**How many problems can you find?**

???
Give the class a minute. Ask for shouts.

---
name: spot_answers

# Spot the problems 🔍

```{r spot.file2, echo=FALSE, comment=""}
cat(readLines("data/slide_loading_data/messy_samples.csv"), sep = "\n")
```

--

1. A **comment line** above the header
2. Columns separated by **`;`**, not `,`
3. **Decimal commas**: `24,1`
4. Three ways to say "missing": `n/a`, `-`, `Undetermined`
5. **`yes`/`no`** instead of `TRUE`/`FALSE`
6. `2-Sep`: a gene name **eaten by Excel** (SEPT2)

---
name: naive

# Just read it?

```{r naive, error=TRUE}
read.csv("data/slide_loading_data/messy_samples.csv")
```

--

R isn't being difficult. It's following the defaults: commas between columns, the first line is the header.

**We need to tell R what the file looks like.**

---
name: fixed

# Tell R how

```{r fixed}
samples <- read.csv2("data/slide_loading_data/messy_samples.csv",   # ; and ,
                     comment.char = "#",                            # skip comments
                     na.strings = c("n/a", "-", "Undetermined"))    # missing
samples$treated <- samples$treated == "yes"                         # TRUE/FALSE
str(samples)
```

--

5 of 6 fixed. `2-Sep` can't be fixed by R: **fix it at the source**.

---
name: paths

# Where is my file?

R looks for files in the **working directory**:

```{r paths, eval=FALSE}
getwd()                          # where am I?
file.exists("data/samples.csv")  # is the file there?
```

--

.pull-left-50[
**Do**

- Use an RStudio **Project**
- Keep data in a `data/` folder
- Use **relative** paths:  
  `"data/samples.csv"`
]

.pull-right-50[
**Don't**

- `setwd()` in your script
- Absolute paths:  
  `"C:/Users/me/Desktop/..."`  
  They only work on your computer.
]

<div style="clear: both;"></div>

.footnote[Error `cannot open file ... No such file or directory`? Check `getwd()` and the spelling.]
.footnote[https://tidyverse.org/blog/2017/12/workflow-vs-script/]

---
name: read_family

# Text files: pick the right reader

| File looks like | Function | Separator | Decimal |
|:----------------|:---------|:---------:|:-------:|
| `24.1,12.5` | `read.csv()` | `,` | `.` |
| `24,1;12,5` | `read.csv2()` | `;` | `,` |
| `24.1⇥12.5` | `read.delim()` | tab | `.` |
| anything else | `read.table(sep = ...)` | you choose | `dec = ...` |

<br>

All return a **data frame**. All are `read.table()` with different defaults.

.footnote[Not sure? Open the file in a **text editor** (not Excel) and look.]

---
name: arguments

# The arguments you'll need

| Argument | Fixes | Example |
|:---------|:------|:--------|
| `header` | is line 1 column names? | `header = TRUE` |
| `sep` | column separator | `sep = "\t"` |
| `dec` | decimal mark | `dec = ","` |
| `na.strings` | how missing is written | `na.strings = c("", "NA", "n/a")` |
| `skip` | lines to ignore at the top | `skip = 3` |
| `comment.char` | comment lines | `comment.char = "#"` |

<br>

Everything else: `?read.table`

---
name: check

# Always check what you read

```{r check}
dim(samples)              # expected number of rows and columns?
head(samples, 3)          # does it look right?
colSums(is.na(samples))   # where are the NAs?
```

.footnote[Also: `str()` (are numbers numbers?), `summary()` (any odd values?).]

---
name: excel

# Excel files

```{r excel, eval=FALSE}
library(readxl)
excel_sheets("data/results.xlsx")                 # which sheets?
results <- read_excel("data/results.xlsx",
                      sheet = "qpcr",             # sheet by name or number
                      skip = 1,                   # skip a title row
                      na = c("", "n/a"))
```

--

.content-box-yellow[
Excel silently changes gene names into dates (`SEPT2` → `2-Sep`, `MARCH1` → `1-Mar`). It happened so often that the genes were **renamed** (`SEPTIN2`, `MARCHF1`). Don't open gene lists in Excel.
]

---
name: other_formats

# Other formats

| Data | Package | Function |
|:-----|:--------|:---------|
| big CSV/TSV, fast | `readr`, `data.table` | `read_csv()`, `fread()` |
| Excel | `readxl` | `read_excel()` |
| GTF, GFF, BED | `rtracklayer` | `import()` |
| FASTA | `Biostrings` | `readDNAStringSet()` |
| SPSS, Stata, SAS | `haven` | `read_sav()`, `read_dta()` |

<br>

Files on the web: give the **URL** instead of a path.

```{r url, eval=FALSE}
read.csv("https://example.org/data/samples.csv")
```

---
name: writing

# Writing data

A table for colleagues, Excel or other programs:

```{r write, eval=FALSE}
write.csv(samples, "results/samples_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.table(samples, "results/samples_clean.tsv", sep = "\t",
            row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
```

--

An R object, to read back into R later:

```{r rds, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(samples, "results/samples_clean.rds")
samples <- readRDS("results/samples_clean.rds")
```

`.rds` keeps everything: types, factor levels, attributes. A CSV keeps only text.

---
name: broken

# When reading fails

```{r broken, error=TRUE}
read.table("data/slide_loading_data/broken_genes.tsv", header = TRUE)
```

--

Which line? Count the fields:

```{r broken2}
count.fields("data/slide_loading_data/broken_genes.tsv", sep = "\t")
readLines("data/slide_loading_data/broken_genes.tsv")[3]
```

TP53 has no `end`. Fix the file, or use `fill = TRUE` to get an `NA`.

.footnote[Careful: `read.csv()` and `read.delim()` use `fill = TRUE` by default, so short rows are padded **silently**.]

---
name: recap

# Recap

| Step | How |
|:-----|:----|
| 1. Look at the file | text editor, `readLines(file, n = 5)` |
| 2. Pick the reader | `read.csv()`, `read.csv2()`, `read.delim()`, `read_excel()` |
| 3. Describe the file | `sep`, `dec`, `na.strings`, `skip`, `comment.char` |
| 4. Check | `dim()`, `str()`, `head()`, `colSums(is.na())` |
| 5. Save | `write.csv(row.names = FALSE)`, `saveRDS()` |

<br>

**Remember:** R reads exactly what you tell it to. Look first, then read, then check.
